title: Estonia Navigates Inflation Relief and Pension Pressure in Dual Economic Test · 05 Sep
keywords: Estonia, inflation, cost of living, pension age, fiscal sustainability, GDP growth, wages, eurozone, retirement reform, ageing population, Baltic economy, social policy
notes: Estonia's economy returned to modest growth in the second quarter of 2026, and inflation has fallen to its lowest level in more than five years, offering households some respite after a prolonged cost-of-living squeeze. Yet the government faces a parallel political battle over plans to raise the retirement age in 2029, a reform officials say is essential to fiscal sustainability but which critics argue places an unequal burden on workers. Together, the two debates define the central tension in Estonian public life: whether stabilisation translates into broad relief, and who bears the cost of an ageing society.
